kaigo-language-session-4-notes.heading: Grooming roles, times and independence: reading points
paragraphs: Ireba and gishi both mean artificial teeth replacing missing teeth. The term alone does not tell who removed them, where they are stored or whether care is complete. Toothbrushing is one part of oral care; completing it does not establish that every necessary oral-care task is finished.

Midashinami means arranging appearance according to cleanliness, preferences and activities. Mijitaku means preparing for upcoming activities through dressing and similar actions. They can overlap but are not interchangeable in every context.

Pantsu can mean trousers or underwear depending on context. Underwear is worn inside clothing. Kigae can mean changing clothes or the replacement clothes themselves; kōi means changing clothes. If a requested item is unclear, ask which garment is meant.

Miru written 診る refers to examination by a physician, dentist or similar professional, unlike 見る for simply looking or observing. Yonaka means the middle of the night. Hearing about an event this morning does not permit recording a nighttime event as occurring in the morning.

A schedule saying “dressing planned” does not establish completed changing. A plan describes intended future action. When adding actors or times, use stated facts or actual checks. Practice explaining: “The plan is known, but implementation is unconfirmed.”

For giving and receiving, distinguish giver, recipient and deliverer. In a learning example, “My friend gave me a postcard” means the friend gave it and the person received it. The person can describe the same event as “I received a postcard from my friend.” Neither sentence identifies who delivered it to the facility.

“Like best” means greatest preference within the comparison. Saying “I like looking at flowers best” does not mean disliking other activities. Today’s chosen activity is not necessarily the usual favorite. Distinguish degree of preference from this occasion’s choice.

kaigo-reading-new-225.heading: Separate schedule preparation, checking and distribution
paragraphs:
Worker A: Who made this dressing schedule?
Worker B: I made it yesterday. The person responsible checked it this morning.
Worker A: Who gave it to the person?
Worker B: Reception staff. I did not take it there.
Worker A: So preparation, checking and distribution involved different people?
Worker B: Yes. The preparation and checking days differ too.

B prepared it yesterday, the person responsible checked it this morning, and reception staff delivered it. B explicitly did not take it. Match each actor and distinguish yesterday from this morning. The conversation does not state whether the person finished changing clothes.

kaigo-reading-new-226.heading: When an item became missing and future checks
paragraphs:
Person: I have not been able to find my denture case since the middle of the night.
Worker: So you did not first notice this morning?
Person: Right. I searched at night and again in the morning.
Worker: I will check with the responsible worker and let you know if it is found.
Person: It has not been found yet?
Worker: Correct. We cannot yet say the storage location is known.

The case has been missing since the middle of the night, with searches at night and in the morning, not first noticed this morning. The worker plans to ask the responsible colleague and notify the person if found. Neither discovery nor storage-location confirmation is complete; do not report either as established.

kaigo-reading-new-227.heading: Outgoing clothes and the jacket to keep
paragraphs:
Person: I want to separate clothes for laundry.
Worker: In the box on the right?
Person: No. The right is for returned clothes. Outgoing clothes go on the left.
Worker: I checked the box labels. I will put them on the left.
Person: Keep the jacket, please. I need it this afternoon.
Worker: I will separate the other clothes without sending the jacket.

Here the right box contains returned clothes and the left is for outgoing laundry. Staff checked labels but did not state sorting is complete. The person wants to keep the afternoon jacket. The response preserves both left/right placement and the exception.

kaigo-reading-new-228.heading: Independent grooming and requested visual feedback
paragraphs:
Worker: I adjusted the mirror angle a little earlier.
Person: Thank you. I can see my face and check my appearance.
Worker: Shall I help arrange your collar too?
Person: I can do the collar. Just tell me how the back looks.
Worker: Understood. I will look and tell you.
Person: I do not need everything done for me.

The worker already adjusted the mirror. The person can arrange the collar, but completion is not stated. They request only observation and description of the back. Neither taking over everything nor providing no help matches the wish.

kaigo-language-session-4-terms.heading: Term reference: grooming roles, times and independence
paragraphs: This reference helps clarify unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not a task to learn every word anew today. Choose today’s useful terms and return when needed.
衣類（いるい） — Clothing: garments worn on the body.
入れ歯（いれば） — Dentures: an everyday word for artificial teeth replacing missing teeth.
うがい（うがい） — Rinsing or gargling: rinsing the mouth or throat; check the specific method and ability according to condition and support.
上着（うわぎ） — Upper garment: clothing worn on the upper body; here, an outer garment such as a jacket.
着替え（きがえ） — Changing clothes; also the clothes prepared for changing.
義歯（ぎし） — Dentures: artificial teeth replacing missing teeth, also called ireba.
起床（きしょう） — Getting up: rising from bed.
くし（くし） — Comb: a tool for combing and arranging hair.
更衣（こうい） — Changing clothes.
口腔ケア（こうくうけあ） — Oral care: care supporting cleanliness and health of the mouth, including teeth and gums.
下着（したぎ） — Underwear: clothing worn beneath outer garments.
スカート（すかーと） — Skirt: a waist-down garment without separate legs.
爪きり（つめきり） — Nail clippers: a tool for cutting nails. In this exercise, learn the name without performing untrained actions.
とかす（とかす） — Comb: here, arrange hair using a comb.
ドライヤー（どらいやー） — Hair dryer: a device that blows air to dry hair. Take care with heat.
ねまき（ねまき） — Nightwear: clothing worn for sleep.
歯医者（はいしゃ） — Dentist: an everyday term for a dental professional, sometimes also a dental clinic.
歯ブラシ（はぶらし） — Toothbrush: a brush for cleaning teeth.
歯磨き（はみがき） — Toothbrushing: cleaning teeth with a toothbrush or similar item.
パンツ（ぱんつ） — Pants or underwear: clarify which is intended when context is unclear.
ひげ剃り（ひげそり） — Shaving: removing facial hair; sometimes also the shaving tool.
みだしなみ（みだしなみ） — Grooming: arranging appearance for cleanliness, personal preferences and activities.
ゆすぐ（ゆすぐ） — Rinse: for the mouth, taking water or similar liquid into it to rinse; check method according to condition.
左側（ひだりがわ） — Left side: left from the reference person or object; check whose viewpoint applies.
右側（みぎがわ） — Right side: right from the reference person or object; check whose viewpoint applies.
診る（みる） — Examine medically: examination by a physician or dentist, distinguished from simply looking.
夜中（よなか） — Middle of the night: read as the event time, separately from when the account was heard.
診察（しんさつ） — Medical examination: a physician or dentist checks health by listening and examining the body. Distinguish this role from care-worker observation.

kaigo-language-session-5-notes.heading: Scope of hygiene help and changed signs: reading points
paragraphs: Even after dressing is finished, another task such as fastening a name badge may remain. Ask what is difficult and how far the person wants to act independently, and confirm consent for necessary help. Permission to assist one part does not mean permission to do everything.

When checking temperature, specify whether it concerns water, room air or an object’s surface. Nurui expresses not very hot or less warm than expected. This word alone cannot determine safe water temperature or device settings. Clarify the difficulty and discuss necessary adjustments with the person responsible.

Bed bathing wipes the body clean, hair washing cleans hair, and face washing cleans the face. A washbasin is a water container, unlike a fixed sink. A bathroom is the bathing room, a bathtub holds water for immersion, and a changing room is for undressing or dressing. Distinguish action from location.

Disinfection processes reduce infection risk by reducing pathogens or similar means; disinfectant is the liquid used. Distinguish action and material. Maintaining cleanliness means preserving a clean condition; that record alone does not prove disinfection. Vocabulary practice does not prescribe disinfectant products or concentrations.

In “checked the hair-washing plan,” the completed action is checking the plan, not washing hair. Read words with several meanings alongside their objects: pouring water, applying brakes and sweating describe different actions.

kaigo-reading-new-229.heading: Help only with the name badge
paragraphs:
Person: I have changed clothes. I also want to attach my name badge.
Worker: Can you use the fastener?
Person: I tried opening it but cannot fasten it properly.
Worker: May I help only with attaching the badge?
Person: Yes. I chose these clothes already; please do not change them.
Worker: Leave the clothes as they are, and just the badge.

Dressing is complete and the person chose the clothes. They opened the fastener to try it but have not fastened the badge. Consent covers badge help without changing clothes. Even at the conversation’s end, attaching the badge is not reported complete.

kaigo-reading-new-231.heading: Larger text and unchecked arrows
paragraphs:
Worker A: The bathroom entrance sign is easier to see than yesterday.
Worker B: The text is larger, but I have not checked the arrows yet.
Worker A: We cannot yet say the entire sign is clearer.
Worker B: Right. I want to ask the person’s opinion too.
Worker A: Let us compare before and after in the record.
Worker B: I will separate text size from unchecked points.

A compares with yesterday’s sign. B confirmed larger text, but arrows remain unchecked and the person’s opinion is still to be asked. One change does not establish clearer guidance overall. Record changes separately from unknowns.

kaigo-reading-new-232.heading: Change start date and today’s wishes
paragraphs:
Person: Yesterday’s notice said the face-washing location will change.
Worker: That starts next week. Today we use the usual place.
Person: So not the new place today?
Worker: Correct. Let us check today’s directions first.
Person: I only want the location now. I want to wash this afternoon.
Worker: Location now, face washing this afternoon.

The change in yesterday’s notice starts next week; today uses the previous location. The person wants only location information now, not immediate washing. Separate the notice-reading day, change start date and preferred activity time.

kaigo-language-session-5-terms.heading: Term reference: hygiene help and sign changes
paragraphs: This reference helps clarify unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not a task to learn every word anew today. Choose today’s useful terms and return when needed.
温度（おんど） — Temperature: degree of hotness or coldness. Identify whether it is room, water or another temperature.
かける（かける） — A context-dependent verb: with hot water it means pouring; with brakes it means applying.
かく（かく） — In “sweat,” it means producing sweat. Distinguish from writing or scratching through context.
シャンプー（しゃんぷー） — Shampoo: a product for washing hair and scalp.
消毒（しょうどく） — Disinfection: reducing infection risk by reducing pathogens or similar means. This is not practice in selecting products or concentrations.
消毒液（しょうどくえき） — Disinfectant solution: liquid for disinfection. Knowing the name differs from judging a suitable product or method.
清潔保持（せいけつほじ） — Maintaining hygiene: keeping necessary cleanliness through methods suited to the person.
清拭（せいしき） — Bed bathing: wiping the body clean with towels or similar items, either fully or partially.
洗髪（せんぱつ） — Hair washing: washing the hair and scalp, separate from completed drying or styling.
洗面（せんめん） — Face washing.
洗面器（せんめんき） — Washbasin: a container for water used to wash face or body, unlike a fixed sink.
脱衣室（だついしつ） — Changing room: a room for undressing or dressing before or after bathing and similar activities.
入浴（にゅうよく） — Bathing: cleaning the body by methods such as entering bathwater. Follow the plan for the specific method.
ぬるい（ぬるい） — Lukewarm: feeling not very hot or less warm than expected, not a numerical safe temperature.
拭く（ふく） — Wipe: remove moisture or dirt with cloth, a towel or a similar item.
浴室（よくしつ） — Bathroom: a room for washing the body or using a bathtub.
浴槽（よくそう） — Bathtub: equipment holding water for immersing the body, not the whole bathroom.
リンス（りんす） — Conditioner: a product used to condition hair during washing.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.

kaigo-language-session-6-notes.heading: Read hygiene explanations through degree, direction and conditions
paragraphs: “Difficult to” does not necessarily mean impossible, and “easy to” expresses ease rather than guaranteed success. Even slip-resistant flooring does not guarantee no slips. Preserve degrees rather than changing them to cannot or certainly can.
For “from…to…” or “toward,” check origin and destination. One-way guidance does not establish the return route or direction. Match symbols such as circles and stars to that diagram’s explanation.

Ask separately what should change and what is acceptable unchanged. “I will check whether it can be changed” means investigation is ahead, not a completed setting change. A request following “if that is not possible” applies under that condition; do not decide the outcome before checking.

“Hard to hear” alone does not establish inability to hear every sound. Check specific difficulties such as speech speed, background sound or location, and ask preferred communication. Here distinguish a requested volume change from a speed change.

kaigo-reading-new-233.heading: Specify the difficult-to-read part
paragraphs:
Person: I can see the changing-room shelf numbers, but they are a little hard to read.
Worker: They are not completely invisible?
Person: Right. The small text below the number is unclear.
Worker: I will check numbers and small text separately.
Person: Please do not say I cannot read any of it.
Worker: I will report difficulty with some parts.

The numbers are visible but somewhat hard to read, particularly the small text underneath. The person asks that this not be reported as total inability. Separate numbers from small text and visibility from reading difficulty, preserving scope and degree.

kaigo-reading-new-234.heading: Origin and destination in one diagram
paragraphs:
Worker A: This arrow goes from the changing room toward reception.
Worker B: Is it not reception to the changing room?
Worker A: No. The circle is the starting point, the star the destination.
Worker B: On this sheet, the circle is the changing room?
Worker A: Yes. There is a separate return-route diagram.
Worker B: I will not assume both diagrams have the same direction.

In this diagram the circle is the changing-room origin and the star the reception destination. The arrow points from changing room to reception. The return route has a separate diagram, so this sheet alone cannot explain it. These symbols belong to this scenario, not a universal facility sign rule.

kaigo-reading-new-235.heading: Change speed, with volume unchanged
paragraphs:
Person: I want bathing instructions, but the recording is too fast.
Worker: Shall I increase the volume?
Person: The volume is fine. I want only the speed changed.
Worker: I will check whether playback can be slowed.
Person: If not, please explain in short sections.
Worker: First I will check settings and tell you the result.

Volume is acceptable; only speed should change. The worker will check whether playback can slow. Short-section explanation is requested if slowing is impossible. Neither a setting change nor explanation is established as complete.

kaigo-reading-new-236.heading: Closed here now, notice in the corridor later
paragraphs:
Person: Please close the curtain while explaining bed bathing.
Worker: You wanted to see the notice too?
Person: Yes, but I will see it in the corridor.
Worker: So not opening it here for the explanation?
Person: Keep it closed here. I want the notice later.
Worker: We will separate the current explanation from the later notice.

The person wants the curtain closed for the explanation here and the notice later in the corridor. The wishes differ in place and time. A wish to see a notice is not consent to open the curtain now. Also distinguish wanting an explanation from consenting to bed bathing itself.

kaigo-language-session-6-terms.heading: Term reference: degree, direction and conditions
paragraphs: This reference helps clarify unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not a task to learn every word anew today. Choose today’s useful terms and return when needed.
〜にくい（〜にくい） — Difficult to do: not a declaration that the action is impossible.
〜やすい（〜やすい） — Easy to do: not a guarantee of success.
〜から〜へ（〜から〜へ） — From…to…: connects origin and destination, without specifying the return route.
〜できるか確認する（〜できるかかくにんする） — Check whether possible: possibility and completion are not established yet.
〜できなければ（〜できなければ） — If not possible: interpret the following wish or method together with this condition.

kaigo-language-session-7-notes.heading: Housework information sources and participation scope
paragraphs: Supply counts, personal wishes and staff responsibilities are separate information. A responsible worker checking supplies does not mean the person expressed wishes. Identify who supplied which information; schedules and inventory cannot replace personal choice.

Kawakasu means actively drying something, kawaku means becoming dry, and hosu means spreading or hanging it for drying. Hanging does not establish that drying is complete. “Dry” alone does not identify who hung it. Do not add a later task absent from the text.
Sweeping and vomiting can both be pronounced haku but differ. Use kanji and context to distinguish broom cleaning from a bodily symptom. Do not misread housework records as symptom records.

An oshibori is a damp cloth mainly for hands, while a mop cleans floors. Housework includes cleaning, laundry and cooking. Cooking means preparing food. Sharing housework experience is also participation; the speaker need not undertake every task.

“Hung the laundry, but it is not dry yet” means hanging is complete and dryness is not. Rewriting this as “put away dry items” removes negation and invents storage. Explain completed action separately from a state not yet reached.

kaigo-reading-new-237.heading: Supply checks differ from personal wishes
paragraphs:
Worker A: I checked bathroom supplies with the person responsible.
Worker B: So the person’s wishes are known too?
Worker A: No, only supply counts. I have not asked wishes.
Worker B: I will ask the person.
Worker A: Yes. Do not decide from the schedule alone.
Worker B: Equipment checks and personal choices are separate.

A checked only supply counts with the responsible worker. Wishes remain unasked, and B will ask the person. Neither a staff check nor a schedule proves personal choice. Supply counts also do not establish health checks or performed care.

kaigo-reading-new-239.heading: Separate counting from carrying
paragraphs:
Worker: We plan to list equipment during the housework activity.
Person: I can help count, but I will not carry things.
Worker: Will you carry them to the shelf after counting?
Person: No, counting only. Please have someone else carry them.
Worker: Understood. I will write the counts on the list.
Person: Please call me when you begin.

The person accepts counting only and refuses carrying. Staff will write counts. Someone else must carry, but no carrier is identified yet. The person wants a call when starting; the task is not established as already underway.

kaigo-reading-new-240.heading: Participation by sharing memories
paragraphs:
Person: For next month’s cooking activity, I want to introduce old menus.
Worker: Do you plan to cook them yourself?
Person: Not cook; I will share memories with everyone.
Worker: We need time to talk with cooking staff too.
Person: Yes. What to cook is not decided yet.
Worker: I will report the introduction wish and undecided menu separately.

The person wants to share old-menu memories next month, not cook personally. Time with cooking staff is needed, but the menu is undecided. Cooking staff have not been stated to accept a dish assignment. Report the wish separately from the undecided menu.

kaigo-language-session-7-terms.heading: Term reference: housework sources and participation
paragraphs: This reference helps clarify unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not a task to learn every word anew today. Choose today’s useful terms and return when needed.
おしぼり（おしぼり） — Damp hand cloth: mainly for wiping hands, distinguished from floor-cleaning equipment.
カーテン（かーてん） — Curtain: fabric covering windows or spaces to adjust light or screen views.
家事（かじ） — Housework: tasks maintaining daily life, such as cooking, cleaning and laundry.
片付ける（かたづける） — Put away: organize items into agreed places, not discard them without permission.
乾かす（かわかす） — Dry something: remove moisture to make it dry, distinguished from becoming dry.
乾く（かわく） — Become dry: reach a dry state as moisture reduces, without identifying an actor or action.
換気（かんき） — Ventilation: replace indoor air with outside air.
シーツ（しーつ） — Sheet: fabric covering bedding.
洗濯物（せんたくもの） — Laundry: items awaiting washing or already washed. Check the processing stage too.
掃除機（そうじき） — Vacuum cleaner: a machine removing dust and debris by suction.
たたむ（たたむ） — Fold: arrange fabric in overlapping layers, distinct from washing or hanging it.
調理（ちょうり） — Cooking: handling ingredients and preparing edible dishes.
掃く（はく） — Sweep: gather or remove dirt with a broom or similar tool, unlike vomiting.
布団（ふとん） — Futon bedding: bedding placed below or above the sleeper; check which through context.
ほうき（ほうき） — Broom: a tool for sweeping floor dirt or dust.
干す（ほす） — Hang or spread out: place things for drying or similar purposes, not necessarily already dry.
枕（まくら） — Pillow: bedding supporting the head during sleep or rest.
毛布（もうふ） — Blanket: bedding used, for example, to cover and warm the body.
モップ（もっぷ） — Mop: a handled cleaning tool with cloth or similar material for wiping floors.

kaigo-language-session-8-notes.heading: Housework conditions, experience and confirmed results
paragraphs: A scheduled time is decided beforehand; actual completion means the activity really ended. When completion of another activity is a condition, the scheduled time alone does not satisfy it. Identify what must be confirmed and with whom before proceeding.
“Could you tell me?” can request an explanation or shared experience rather than delegation of an entire job. If unclear, specify whether you want to hear ideas or ask for actual work.

When marks indicate completed areas, confirmation applies to those areas only. Do not extend it to all work. If unmarked areas are unchecked, do not declare them unfinished either. Thank the person while recording the known scope accurately.
Practice: “Marked areas are complete. Unmarked areas have not been checked.” Do not replace unknown with impossible, refused or complete. Consider what needs checking for the next judgment.

kaigo-reading-new-241.heading: Check actual activity completion rather than scheduled noon
paragraphs:
Worker A: Someone raised concern about vacuum noise.
Worker B: Use it at noon?
Worker A: Not by time alone. First confirm the neighboring activity has ended.
Worker B: It is scheduled until noon, but it could run late.
Worker A: Yes. Ask the responsible worker to confirm completion.
Worker B: I will separate scheduled time from actual completion.

Here vacuum use requires the neighboring activity’s actual end. Noon is scheduled, but an extension is possible. The assigned check is to ask the responsible worker before use. This scenario condition is not a universal rule banning vacuuming until noon.

kaigo-reading-new-242.heading: A request to share experience
paragraphs:
Person: I have ideas for arranging clothes so they are easier to find.
Worker: Could you tell me about them?
Person: Am I to put everything away?
Worker: No. I want your ideas, not to assign you the job.
Person: Then I will explain arranging by order of use.
Worker: After organizing what you tell me, we will discuss actual placement.

Staff request ideas for finding clothes, not complete tidying. The person will explain order-of-use arrangement; staff will organize the information before discussing placement. Neither changed arrangement nor consent to it is stated.

kaigo-reading-new-243.heading: Marked and unchecked areas
paragraphs:
Person: I marked completed areas on the tidying schedule.
Worker: Thank you. Are unmarked areas finished too?
Person: I have not looked there yet.
Worker: Now we can identify finished areas.
Person: Yes. Please do not write that everything is done.
Worker: I will record marked and unchecked areas separately.

The person marked finished areas and has not inspected unmarked ones. The marks identify completed parts only. Neither all-complete nor unmarked-incomplete is established. Staff thank the person and distinguish completion from unknowns.

kaigo-language-session-8-terms.heading: Term reference: housework conditions and results
paragraphs: This reference helps clarify unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not a task to learn every word anew today. Choose today’s useful terms and return when needed.
予定時刻（よていじこく） — Scheduled time: decided beforehand, distinguished from actual start or finish time.
終了（しゅうりょう） — Completion: an activity ending; planned completion is not actual completion.
工夫（くふう） — Practical idea: thinking of or improving methods to suit a purpose.
印（しるし） — Mark: a symbol used as an indicator; check its meaning in the table’s explanation.
未確認（みかくにん） — Unconfirmed: not checked yet, rather than refused or impossible.

kaigo-language-session-9-notes.heading: Separate state, time and unknowns in handoffs
paragraphs: When reading handoffs, distinguish choices, actions needing help and matters not yet asked. Choosing clothes differs from dressing alone. Support for independence values both choice and action-specific help.

Observation carefully checks condition and changes; reporting conveys known information to necessary recipients; handoff passes needed information to continuing staff. “Report sent” alone does not establish receipt or completed action.
A plan determines future actions; a change alters its content. A participant joins an activity; a service user uses services. A name on a plan does not establish consent or actual participation.

Case can mean a container or a situation. Ryuko can mean infection spread or popular styles. Monitoring checks condition so necessary help can be arranged; the term alone does not establish complete independence.
Going to bed, going to work and finishing work describe different events. Day and night shifts indicate work periods. Separate report creation time from the recorded event time.

“Changed the medication schedule” reports a plan change, not medication taken. This reading practice does not authorize independently changing medication instructions. When studying call buttons, alarms or 119, do not activate real equipment or call emergency services for practice.

kaigo-reading-new-247.heading: Independent choice and dressing assistance
paragraphs:
Handoff about the person
For morning dressing, the person chooses the type of jacket. Staff help put the arms through sleeves.
On some afternoon activity days the jacket is not changed. Wishes about changing this afternoon have not been asked yet.
Check independent choice separately from dressing alone.

The person chooses jacket type and staff assist sleeves. Choice does not establish independence in every dressing action. Some afternoons involve no change, but today’s wish is unasked. Do not infer today’s choice from usual patterns.

kaigo-reading-new-248.heading: Recorded facts and unstated reasons
paragraphs:
Activity record
Last week’s visit was shorter than scheduled. The reason is not recorded.
Today the person is talking with staff in the lounge, not visiting family.
In large-group activities they sometimes ask to hear explanations again. So far, today’s two-person conversation has no such request.
Afternoon event participation will be checked with the person.

Last week’s visit shortened for an unstated reason. Today is conversation with staff, not family. Repetition sometimes occurs in large groups but not so far in today’s pair conversation. Preserve conditions and time rather than generalizing hearing. Afternoon wishes remain to be asked.

kaigo-language-session-9-terms.heading: Term reference: handoff state, time and unknowns
paragraphs: This reference helps clarify unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not a task to learn every word anew today. Choose today’s useful terms and return when needed.
観察（かんさつ） — Observation: carefully checking the person and surroundings.
行事（ぎょうじ） — Event: a planned gathering or activity.
禁止（きんし） — Prohibition: something specified as not allowed. Read the location and time scope too.
計画（けいかく） — Plan: agreed future actions, methods and timing toward a goal.
掲示（けいじ） — Notice: displaying information visibly, or the document displayed.
ケース（けーす） — Case: may mean a container, example or situation.
玄関（げんかん） — Entrance: a place for entering and leaving a building.
参加者（さんかしゃ） — Participant: someone joining an activity; distinguish planned and actual participation.
事故（じこ） — Accident: an unintended event leading to injury, damage or similar harm.
施設（しせつ） — Facility: a building, equipment or organization providing support or services.
就寝（しゅうしん） — Going to bed: entering bed to sleep.
出勤（しゅっきん） — Going to work: going to the workplace for duty.
巡視（じゅんし） — Rounds: going around designated areas to check conditions.
使用（しよう） — Use: using an item or facility.
状況（じょうきょう） — Situation: circumstances of people or things at that time.
ショートステイ（しょーとすてい） — Short stay: staying briefly in a facility with needed support. Check service conditions with the consultation contact.
自立（じりつ） — Independence: acting with one’s own abilities and choosing and deciding how to live.
送迎車（そうげいしゃ） — Pick-up/drop-off vehicle: transport used to collect or take service users or others.
退勤（たいきん） — Leaving work: finishing the day’s duty and returning home.
タイヤ（たいや） — Tire: the part covering the outside of a vehicle wheel.
建物（たてもの） — Building: a structure people enter to live or undertake activities.
担当者（たんとうしゃ） — Person responsible: someone assigned to a task or support.
調理員（ちょうりいん） — Cooking staff: workers responsible for preparing meals.
転倒（てんとう） — Fall: losing balance and falling during standing, walking or a similar activity.
ナースコール（なーすこーる） — Call system: equipment for contacting staff and requesting help. Do not operate real equipment for this lesson.
日勤（にっきん） — Day shift: work mainly during daytime; check exact hours in the workplace schedule.
濡れる（ぬれる） — Become wet: acquire water or another liquid.
吐く（はく） — Vomit or expel: return stomach contents or release breath or material through the mouth; identify the object from context.
外す（はずす） — Remove: detach or take off an attached item.
非常口（ひじょうぐち） — Emergency exit: an exit for escape during fire or other emergencies.
非常ベル（ひじょうべる） — Emergency alarm: equipment signaling fire or another emergency; never activate it for practice.
119番（ひゃくじゅうきゅうばん） — 119: Japan’s emergency number for fire engines or ambulances; do not call to test connection or for learning.
服薬（ふくやく） — Taking medication: distinguish it from plans or plan changes.
変更（へんこう） — Change: alter something decided. Also check what remains unchanged.
報告（ほうこく） — Report: communicate confirmed facts, actions, results or changes.
ホール（ほーる） — Hall: a large room or space for gatherings; the specific location varies by facility.
まつり（まつり） — Festival: an event or celebration in a community or facility.
ミーティング（みーてぃんぐ） — Meeting: staff or others gathering to share information or discuss.
見守り（みまもり） — Monitoring: checking condition and actions so needed support can be provided; not complete independence.
面会（めんかい） — Visit: meeting the person in person, unlike letter or telephone contact.
申し送り（もうしおくり） — Handoff: communicate and check conditions, responses and unfinished matters with the next worker to continue support.
夜勤（やきん） — Night shift: work including nighttime; check exact hours in the workplace schedule.
流行（りゅうこう） — Spread or popularity: infection spreading or styles becoming common; distinguish meanings through context.
利用者（りようしゃ） — Person receiving services: someone using care or other services.

kaigo-language-session-10-notes.heading: Record conditions, roles and privacy
paragraphs: Recorded ability may depend on glasses or quiet surroundings. Do not remove those conditions and assume equal ability everywhere. “Not tried today” proves neither inability nor ability.

For activity records, identify who chose, acted and supported each part. A family offer need not match personal wishes. Staff reading letters or sharing private content requires separate checking with the person; respect wishes and sharing scope.

When organizing information, separate completed facts, statements by the person or family and unasked matters. Do not change “not yet asked” into refusal or inability. Respecting statements is compatible with identifying unknowns.

kaigo-reading-new-249.heading: Conditions for readable text and understandable speech
paragraphs:
Reading-activity record
Text: Large text can be read with glasses. Small text was not tried today.
Audio: In a quiet room, explanations are heard at ordinary volume. Corridor announcements are reportedly difficult to understand.
Choice: Ask whether the person wants larger text or staff reading.

Large text is readable with glasses; small text was not tested today. Ordinary voice works in a quiet room, while corridor announcements are difficult. Preserve text size, glasses, location and sound type. Enlarging text or staff reading remains a future choice to ask about.

kaigo-reading-new-250.heading: Gardening actions by person and task
paragraphs:
Gardening participation record
Pot choice: The person chose the color.
Label: The person wrote the name; staff wrote the date.
Tidying: The equipment carrier is undecided.
Next time: Check the preferred role before participation.

The person chose the pot color and wrote the name; staff wrote the date. The carrier is undecided, and next-time role wishes will be checked before participation. Doing some parts does not establish doing everything or a decided future role.

kaigo-reading-new-251.heading: Personal wishes, sister’s offer and unconfirmed consent
paragraphs:
Communication-preference interview
The person wants to correspond with their younger sister by letter. Visiting wishes have not been asked.
The sister said by phone she could send envelopes. They have not arrived.
Whether staff may read the letter also requires confirmation with the person.

The person wants letters with their younger sister. The sister offered envelopes by phone, but none have arrived. Visiting wishes and consent to staff reading remain unconfirmed. Do not replace personal wishes or consent with the sister’s offer; ask about handling private letter content.

kaigo-language-session-10-terms.heading: Term reference: conditions, roles and privacy
paragraphs: This reference helps clarify unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not a task to learn every word anew today. Choose today’s useful terms and return when needed.
条件（じょうけん） — Conditions: circumstances or prerequisites, including locations or equipment.
役割（やくわり） — Role: an assigned task; distinguish choosing, writing, carrying and other actions.
希望（きぼう） — Wishes: what the person would like to do or have happen.
申し出（もうしで） — Offer or statement: conveying ideas or what one can do, not necessarily completed action.
未確認（みかくにん） — Unconfirmed: not checked yet, rather than refused or impossible.
同意（どうい） — Consent: accepting something after explanation or similar information; it does not automatically extend to other acts.

148.title: Grooming roles, times and independence
objectives: Distinguish preparation, checking and distribution actors and times.
Read independent actions and desired grooming help separately.
148.context: Four conversations concern dressing schedules, a denture case, laundry and a mirror. Check actors, actions and unfinished parts.
148.artCaption: The person selects clothes while staff show them. Check choice separately from dressing assistance.

149.title: Scope of hygiene help and changed signs
objectives: Do not confuse consent to one part with complete performance.
Distinguish change start dates, today’s wishes and checked versus unknown points.
149.context: Study badge help and bathroom or washing directions. Connect vocabulary with the actual requested actions.
149.artCaption: Staff listen face to face. Practice checking wishes and assistance scope before action.

150.title: Read hygiene explanations through degree, direction and conditions
objectives: Preserve reading difficulty rather than reporting total inability.
Distinguish route direction, requested changes and conditional requests.
150.context: Shelf labels, routes, recording speed and curtains illustrate preserving place, time and degree.
150.artCaption: Staff prepare a basin and towels. Preparation does not show technique, water temperature or consent to care.

151.title: Housework information sources and participation scope
objectives: Separate supply checks, wishes and task assignments.
Distinguish sharing experience from performing work.
151.context: Read equipment and participation conversations, identifying sources without replacing wishes with other information.
151.artCaption: Staff listen near glasses on a table. Consent to wiping does not necessarily extend to moving objects.

152.title: Housework conditions, experience and confirmed results
objectives: Distinguish scheduled time from actual completion.
Separate advice requests from work requests and completion from unknowns.
152.context: Vacuum conditions, tidying ideas and schedule marks combine appreciation with accurate records.
152.artCaption: The person demonstrates handling a bag. Sharing experience differs from assigning all work.

153.title: Separate state, time and unknowns in handoffs
objectives: Read choice separately from assistance needs.
Preserve observation conditions and unasked preferences.
153.context: Read dressing handoffs and activity records without inventing unstated reasons or participation wishes.
153.artCaption: Two staff discuss documents. Organize reported information and receiver checks.

154.title: Record conditions, roles and privacy
objectives: Read conditions for understanding text and speech.
Distinguish personal and family offers, actors and unconfirmed consent.
154.context: Reading, gardening and letter records show specific abilities and wishes without inferring consent from family words.
154.artCaption: The person and staff discuss documents, checking wishes and scope before reading or sharing private content.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-225.prompt: Who gave the schedule to the person?
options: Reception staff, a different person from its creator B.
B created it yesterday and delivered it.
The worker checking it this morning delivered it.
Reception staff only checked it this morning.
rationales: B created yesterday, the responsible worker checked this morning, and reception distributed. These actors remain distinct.
B explicitly did not take it; creation and delivery cannot be merged.
The responsible worker checked; reception delivered.
Reception handed it over; someone else checked this morning.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-225.reading:
Worker A: Who made this dressing schedule?
Worker B: I made it yesterday. The person responsible checked it this morning.
Worker A: Who gave it to the person?
Worker B: Reception staff. I did not take it there.
Worker A: So preparation, checking and distribution involved different people?
Worker B: Yes. The preparation and checking days differ too.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-226.prompt: What is currently confirmed about the case?
options: First noticed this morning and searched only then.
Storage was confirmed and the person informed.
Not found at night but found in the morning.
Missing since the middle of the night; staff will ask the responsible worker.
rationales: Searches occurred at night and morning; do not change onset to morning.
Checking and later notification are future actions; storage is unknown.
A morning search is not discovery, and staff confirm it remains missing.
The nighttime onset and searches are known; checking, discovery and storage confirmation are not complete.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-226.reading:
Person: I have not been able to find my denture case since the middle of the night.
Worker: So you did not first notice this morning?
Person: Right. I searched at night and again in the morning.
Worker: I will check with the responsible worker and let you know if it is found.
Person: It has not been found yet?
Worker: Correct. We cannot yet say the storage location is known.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-227.prompt: Which sorting matches the person’s wishes?
options: Put all laundry, including the afternoon jacket, left.
Keep the jacket and separate other outgoing clothes on the left.
Keep the jacket and put outgoing clothes in the right box.
Move returned clothes left and send only the jacket.
rationales: Left is correct, but the jacket must stay for afternoon use.
Left is outgoing, right returned, and the jacket exception is preserved.
Right is returned clothes, not outgoing laundry.
Left is outgoing, while the jacket must stay; action and object are wrong.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-227.reading:
Person: I want to separate clothes for laundry.
Worker: In the box on the right?
Person: No. The right is for returned clothes. Outgoing clothes go on the left.
Worker: I checked the box labels. I will put them on the left.
Person: Keep the jacket, please. I need it this afternoon.
Worker: I will separate the other clothes without sending the jacket.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-228.prompt: What help does the person request?
options: They arrange the collar; staff describe the back.
Staff will adjust mirror and collar entirely.
Only collar help, with back observation refused.
Independent collar care means no back feedback needed.
rationales: This matches independent collar care and requested back feedback.
The mirror is already adjusted; full grooming was not requested.
This reverses requested and independent parts.
One independent action does not remove the requested support.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-228.reading:
Worker: I adjusted the mirror angle a little earlier.
Person: Thank you. I can see my face and check my appearance.
Worker: Shall I help arrange your collar too?
Person: I can do the collar. Just tell me how the back looks.
Worker: Understood. I will look and tell you.
Person: I do not need everything done for me.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-229.prompt: What scope of help was agreed?
options: Staff reselect clothes to ease badge attachment.
Only open the fastener, refusing badge attachment.
Keep chosen clothes and help only attach the badge.
Redo dressing from the beginning, then attach the badge.
rationales: The person explicitly wants clothes unchanged; consent cannot expand.
They tried opening but could not fasten, then accepted attachment help.
Consent is badge-only with clothes unchanged; actual attachment is still not reported complete.
Dressing is already finished; restarting is outside consent.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-229.reading:
Person: I have changed clothes. I also want to attach my name badge.
Worker: Can you use the fastener?
Person: I tried opening it but cannot fasten it properly.
Worker: May I help only with attaching the badge?
Person: Yes. I chose these clothes already; please do not change them.
Worker: Leave the clothes as they are, and just the badge.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-231.prompt: Which separates confirmed and unchecked sign information?
options: Text and arrows checked, so all guidance improved.
Text enlarged; arrows and personal feedback will be checked.
Text size unknown, but the person said it is clearer.
Clearer arrows remove text-size checks.
rationales: Only size was checked; this generalizes one part to the whole.
This preserves size change and outstanding arrows and feedback checks.
B confirmed larger text; feedback is still future.
Arrows are unchecked; size and arrows are not interchangeable.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-231.reading:
Worker A: The bathroom entrance sign is easier to see than yesterday.
Worker B: The text is larger, but I have not checked the arrows yet.
Worker A: We cannot yet say the entire sign is clearer.
Worker B: Right. I want to ask the person’s opinion too.
Worker A: Let us compare before and after in the record.
Worker B: I will separate text size from unchecked points.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-232.prompt: Which combines today’s place with preferred washing time?
options: New place today and wash immediately.
Change next week means no face washing today.
Usual place, with immediate-washing consent.
Usual place, with face washing wanted this afternoon.
rationales: Change starts next week; now only location is wanted.
The person wants washing this afternoon, not no washing.
The place is correct but desired washing time is afternoon.
This preserves next-week change, location check now and washing later.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-232.reading:
Person: Yesterday’s notice said the face-washing location will change.
Worker: That starts next week. Today we use the usual place.
Person: So not the new place today?
Worker: Correct. Let us check today’s directions first.
Person: I only want the location now. I want to wash this afternoon.
Worker: Location now, face washing this afternoon.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-233.prompt: Which report accurately preserves the person’s account?
options: Neither number nor small text is visible at all.
Visible numbers mean no reading difficulty.
Numbers are visible, but parts such as small text are hard to read.
Only small text is readable; numbers are invisible.
rationales: This changes partial difficulty into total invisibility.
Visible numbers coexist with difficulty reading small text.
This preserves both visible numbers and the scope and degree of difficulty.
The objects and difficulty are reversed.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-233.reading:
Person: I can see the changing-room shelf numbers, but they are a little hard to read.
Worker: They are not completely invisible?
Person: Right. The small text below the number is unclear.
Worker: I will check numbers and small text separately.
Person: Please do not say I cannot read any of it.
Worker: I will report difficulty with some parts.

options: Circle-marked changing room to star-marked reception.
Circle-marked reception to star-marked changing room.
Star reception back to circle changing room.
Both outbound and return routes on one sheet.
rationales: Circle is origin and here means changing room; star means reception.
This reverses the diagram’s location mapping.
The return route is separate; this arrow goes toward reception.
Do not add a return route to a one-way diagram.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-234.reading:
Worker A: This arrow goes from the changing room toward reception.
Worker B: Is it not reception to the changing room?
Worker A: No. The circle is the starting point, the star the destination.
Worker B: On this sheet, the circle is the changing room?
Worker A: Yes. There is a separate return-route diagram.
Worker B: I will not assume both diagrams have the same direction.

options: Whether volume can increase further.
Whether the already-slowed recording was heard to the end.
Whether the already-separated explanation was understood.
Whether recording playback can be slowed.
rationales: Volume is fine; only speed is requested.
Changing settings and later playback checks have not occurred.
Short sections are conditional on inability to slow; no explanation is complete.
First check settings; short explanations follow only if slowing is unavailable.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-235.reading:
Person: I want bathing instructions, but the recording is too fast.
Worker: Shall I increase the volume?
Person: The volume is fine. I want only the speed changed.
Worker: I will check whether playback can be slowed.
Person: If not, please explain in short sections.
Worker: First I will check settings and tell you the result.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-236.prompt: Which preserves both curtain and notice wishes?
options: Open here now because the notice is wanted.
Explain with curtains closed now; see the notice later in the corridor.
Closed curtains mean canceling the notice.
See the corridor notice immediately, then return for explanation.
rationales: A notice wish is not consent to open here now.
Separating place and time preserves both wishes.
The later corridor request remains explicit.
This invents an unrequested order.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-236.reading:
Person: Please close the curtain while explaining bed bathing.
Worker: You wanted to see the notice too?
Person: Yes, but I will see it in the corridor.
Worker: So not opening it here for the explanation?
Person: Keep it closed here. I want the notice later.
Worker: We will separate the current explanation from the later notice.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-237.prompt: What did A confirm with the responsible worker?
options: Only bathroom supply counts; wishes are unasked.
Counts and the person’s chosen use.
Wishes; supply counts are future.
Wishes in the schedule, with questions already asked.
rationales: B will ask wishes; equipment checks and personal choices remain separate.
A explicitly checked counts only.
Confirmed and unconfirmed are reversed.
A says wishes are unasked and not to decide from the schedule.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-237.reading:
Worker A: I checked bathroom supplies with the person responsible.
Worker B: So the person’s wishes are known too?
Worker A: No, only supply counts. I have not asked wishes.
Worker B: I will ask the person.
Worker A: Yes. Do not decide from the schedule alone.
Worker B: Equipment checks and personal choices are separate.

options: The person counts and writes; staff are assigned carrying.
The person counts and carries; staff write.
The person counts, staff write, and someone else must carry.
The person only carries while staff count.
rationales: Staff write and no carrier is assigned yet.
The person refused carrying.
This preserves counting-only participation and staff writing; carrier remains undecided.
Accepted counting and refused carrying are reversed.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-239.reading:
Worker: We plan to list equipment during the housework activity.
Person: I can help count, but I will not carry things.
Worker: Will you carry them to the shelf after counting?
Person: No, counting only. Please have someone else carry them.
Worker: Understood. I will write the counts on the list.
Person: Please call me when you begin.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-240.prompt: How does the person want to participate next month?
options: Cook old dishes while cooking staff watch.
Share old-menu memories, rather than cook personally.
The menu is decided and the person requests cooking.
Cooking staff share memories while the person waits.
rationales: The person explicitly wants talking rather than cooking.
This preserves memory-sharing participation and the undecided menu.
Menu and implementation requests are not established.
The person, not cooking staff, wants to share memories.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-240.reading:
Person: For next month’s cooking activity, I want to introduce old menus.
Worker: Do you plan to cook them yourself?
Person: Not cook; I will share memories with everyone.
Worker: We need time to talk with cooking staff too.
Person: Yes. What to cook is not decided yet.
Worker: I will report the introduction wish and undecided menu separately.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-241.prompt: What is the condition for vacuum use here?
options: Noon, the scheduled finish.
Checking the schedule says noon.
No further complaints about noise.
Confirming the neighboring activity’s actual end with its responsible worker.
rationales: The activity may run late; clock time alone is insufficient.
Scheduled completion does not establish actual completion.
Noise concerns are background, not a complaint-count condition.
This preserves actual completion rather than scheduled noon as the condition.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-241.reading:
Worker A: Someone raised concern about vacuum noise.
Worker B: Use it at noon?
Worker A: Not by time alone. First confirm the neighboring activity has ended.
Worker B: It is scheduled until noon, but it could run late.
Worker A: Yes. Ask the responsible worker to confirm completion.
Worker B: I will separate scheduled time from actual completion.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-242.prompt: What does the staff request “Could you tell me?” mean here?
options: Assign all clothing tidying to the person.
Immediately rearrange according to staff decisions.
Explain ideas for making clothes easier to find.
Test ability to find clothes and report results.
rationales: Staff explicitly want ideas, not delegation.
Placement will be discussed after organizing the ideas; no method is decided.
This distinguishes experience sharing from assigning work.
The request is for ideas, not an ability test or results report.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-242.reading:
Person: I have ideas for arranging clothes so they are easier to find.
Worker: Could you tell me about them?
Person: Am I to put everything away?
Worker: No. I want your ideas, not to assign you the job.
Person: Then I will explain arranging by order of use.
Worker: After organizing what you tell me, we will discuss actual placement.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-243.prompt: Which record of schedule marks is accurate?
options: Marked areas are complete; unmarked areas are unchecked.
Marked areas complete; all unmarked incomplete.
Marking completed areas proves all tidying finished.
Unmarked unknowns make marked completion unknown too.
rationales: This matches completed marks and uninspected areas.
Unconfirmed differs from incomplete.
Only marked parts are established; the person rejects a whole-task claim.
This wrongly extends some unknowns to confirmed parts.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-243.reading:
Person: I marked completed areas on the tidying schedule.
Worker: Thank you. Are unmarked areas finished too?
Person: I have not looked there yet.
Worker: Now we can identify finished areas.
Person: Yes. Please do not write that everything is done.
Worker: I will record marked and unchecked areas separately.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-247.prompt: What is known about this afternoon’s dressing?
options: Choosing a jacket proves complete independence.
Sometimes no change means no change decided today.
Morning sleeve help establishes afternoon consent.
Today’s afternoon wish has not been asked.
rationales: Choice and performance differ, and today’s wish is unknown.
Usual patterns do not establish today’s choice.
Morning help does not establish afternoon wishes or consent.
This preserves the explicitly unasked afternoon preference.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-247.reading:
Handoff about the person
For morning dressing, the person chooses the type of jacket. Staff help put the arms through sleeves.
On some afternoon activity days the jacket is not changed. Wishes about changing this afternoon have not been asked yet.
Check independent choice separately from dressing alone.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-248.prompt: Which reads the activity record correctly?
options: Last week’s visit shortened because explanations were hard to hear.
Today is staff conversation; afternoon participation remains unconfirmed.
No repetition today means none in large groups.
Today is family visiting and afternoon attendance is decided.
rationales: The reason is unstated; this imports information from another setting.
Today is not a family visit and afternoon wishes are still to be checked.
One pair conversation does not negate large-group difficulties.
Both the conversation partner and participation state are wrong.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-248.reading:
Activity record
Last week’s visit was shorter than scheduled. The reason is not recorded.
Today the person is talking with staff in the lounge, not visiting family.
In large-group activities they sometimes ask to hear explanations again. So far, today’s two-person conversation has no such request.
Afternoon event participation will be checked with the person.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-249.prompt: Which preserves the recorded reading conditions?
options: Large text is readable with glasses; small text was not tried today.
Reading large text proves small text readable.
Untested small text proves total inability to read.
Large text is equally readable without glasses.
rationales: This preserves both the confirmed conditions and untested limit.
This extends a confirmed ability into an untested one.
Large text with glasses is established; untested is not impossible.
Glasses are a stated condition; absence was not checked.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-249.reading:
Reading-activity record
Text: Large text can be read with glasses. Small text was not tried today.
Audio: In a quiet room, explanations are heard at ordinary volume. Corridor announcements are reportedly difficult to understand.
Choice: Ask whether the person wants larger text or staff reading.

options: Writing the name proves the person wrote the date.
The person chose color; staff wrote name and date.
The person chose color and wrote the name; staff wrote the date.
The person assigned carrying and chose the same role next time.
rationales: Staff wrote the date; one action does not identify another actor.
The name was the person’s action, not staff’s.
This matches each selection and writing action with its actual actor.
Carrying and future role wishes remain undecided.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-250.reading:
Gardening participation record
Pot choice: The person chose the color.
Label: The person wrote the name; staff wrote the date.
Tidying: The equipment carrier is undecided.
Next time: Check the preferred role before participation.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-251.prompt: Which separates known and unknown letter-contact information?
options: The sister’s envelope offer establishes consent to staff reading.
The person wants letters with the sister; staff reading is unconfirmed.
Wanting letters means refusing visits.
Envelopes arrived and letter writing began.
rationales: The offer concerns envelopes, not the person’s reading consent.
Letter preference is known; envelopes, visiting wishes and reading permission remain outstanding.
Visits were not asked about; letter preference is not refusal.
Arrival and writing are invented from an offer.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-251.reading:
Communication-preference interview
The person wants to correspond with their younger sister by letter. Visiting wishes have not been asked.
The sister said by phone she could send envelopes. They have not arrived.
Whether staff may read the letter also requires confirmation with the person.
